checklist.step: Extract policy, in-force and claims data as of the valuation date
actions: Pull the in-force life/annuity extract (or open the claim triangle for P&C) from the Policy Administration Platform / Claims Platform as of the valuation cutoff date.
Ask the Data Quality Analyst to run the standard data-quality checks (missing dates of birth, negative reserves, out-of-range factors) and return the exception report.
Reconcile record counts and total sums insured/premium to the prior quarter's closing extract; investigate any variance over 1%.
Load the validated extract into the actuarial modeling platform's staging area and tag it with the valuation date.
checklist.done: the extract is data-quality-cleared, reconciled to the prior period within tolerance, and staged in the modeling platform under the valuation-date tag.

checklist.step: Set and document the valuation assumptions
actions: Open the assumption library in FIS Prophet (life) or Milliman Arius (P&C) and pull forward the prior period's mortality/morbidity/lapse or loss-development assumptions.
Compare each assumption to the latest experience study from the Actuarial Analyst and to CIA-published mortality/improvement scales; record any proposed change with rationale.
Route material assumption changes (greater than 2% reserve impact) to the Chief Actuary for pre-approval before loading.
Lock the approved assumption set in the model governance repository with a version tag and effective date.
checklist.done: assumptions are loaded, compared to experience, pre-approved where material, and version-locked in the model governance repository.

checklist.step: Run the CALM/IFRS 17 fulfilment cash flow projection (life) or discounted unpaid-claim projection (P&C)
actions: Execute the production valuation run against the locked assumption set and the staged policy/claims extract.
For life business, confirm the run applies the Canadian Asset Liability Method (CALM)/IFRS 17 fulfilment cash flow approach with the OSFI-prescribed discount curve.
For P&C business, confirm the run applies discounted central estimates by accident/underwriting year from the latest loss-development triangles.
Capture the run log (model version, assumption version, run duration, convergence status) and attach it to the valuation workpaper.
checklist.done: the production run completes on the locked model/assumption versions with a clean convergence log attached to the workpaper.

checklist.step: Compute the Provision for Adverse Deviation (PfAD) / risk margin
actions: Apply the CIA Standards of Practice prescribed PfAD ranges (mortality, morbidity, lapse, expense, interest) to the best-estimate cash flows for life business, or the margin for adverse deviation on unpaid claims for P&C.
Document the selected point within each prescribed range and the rationale, by line of business and product group.
Have the Valuation Actuary independently spot-check three product groups' PfAD selections against the CIA range tables.
Record total PfAD/margin as a separate line in the valuation workpaper.
checklist.done: PfAD/margin is computed within CIA-prescribed ranges, independently spot-checked, and shown as a separate workpaper line.

checklist.step: Reconcile modeled reserves to the general ledger
actions: Extract the current reserve balance by product/GL account from the ERP general ledger.
Match to the modeled reserve output by product/GL mapping and investigate any break greater than the Controller's materiality threshold.
Document reconciling items (in-force movement, currency translation, model timing) with a dollar amount and explanation for each.
Obtain the Controller's sign-off that the reconciliation is complete before reserves are posted.
checklist.done: modeled reserves reconcile to the GL within the materiality threshold, every reconciling item is explained, and Controller sign-off is obtained.

checklist.step: Peer review the valuation run
actions: Independently re-run a materiality-weighted sample of product groups (minimum 20% of reserve balance) in a parallel model instance.
Compare peer-review output to the production run; log any variance beyond tolerance as a review finding.
Check assumption version, discount curve version and model formulae against the locked, approved versions.
Sign and date the peer review checklist before the run proceeds to certification.
checklist.done: the peer reviewer has independently reproduced a materiality-weighted sample within tolerance and signed the review checklist.

checklist.step: Assess reserve adequacy against the prior period and management's best estimate
actions: Decompose the reserve movement from the prior valuation date into new business, in-force runoff, assumption changes, and experience gains/losses, by product.
Compare the modeled reserve to the actuary's independent judgement of adequacy, drawing on the latest experience study and industry benchmarks.
Flag any product group where the movement is unexplained or adequacy judgement diverges from the model beyond the documented threshold.
Record the adequacy conclusion in the valuation memo.
checklist.done: reserve movement is fully decomposed and the Appointed Actuary has recorded an explicit adequacy conclusion for every product group.

checklist.step: Prepare the reserve certification memo
actions: Draft the valuation memorandum stating methodology, assumptions, PfAD selections, reconciliation results, peer review outcome and adequacy conclusion.
Cite the CIA Standards of Practice sections and OSFI Guideline E-15 provisions relied on for the methodology.
Attach the run logs, assumption version tags and reconciliation workpaper as memo exhibits.
Sign and date the memo as the formal reserve certification for the period.
checklist.done: a signed, dated valuation memorandum with methodology, assumptions, reconciliation and adequacy conclusion exists with all exhibits attached.

checklist.step: Obtain Chief Actuary and CFO capital sign-off
actions: Present the reserve movement, PfAD and capital impact (LICAT/MCT ratio effect) to the Chief Financial Officer's capital management team.
Walk through every product group flagged in the adequacy assessment and confirm its disposition.
Obtain written sign-off from the Chief Financial Officer confirming the reserve figures are approved for GL posting and capital reporting.
Log the sign-off date on the valuation workpaper.
checklist.done: the Chief Financial Officer has signed off in writing on the reserve figures and their capital impact before posting.

checklist.step: Post the reserve journal entries
actions: Enter the approved reserve movement journal entry in the ERP general ledger against the signed-off valuation workpaper reference number.
Route the entry through the standard month-end approval workflow for second-person review.
Confirm the posted balance matches the certified reserve figure exactly.
Close the reserve sub-ledger for the period.
checklist.done: the reserve journal entry is posted, second-reviewed, and ties exactly to the certified figure.

checklist.step: Update the model and assumption change log
actions: Record every model version, assumption version and methodology change used in the period in the model governance repository.
Tag each change with its reserve dollar impact and its approver.
Cross-reference the change log entry to the valuation memo exhibit number.
Flag any change that requires model risk validation before its next use.
checklist.done: every model/assumption change for the period is logged, dollar-tagged, cross-referenced and flagged for validation where required.

checklist.step: File the reserve figures into OSFI's regulatory return
actions: Log in to OSFI's Regulatory Reporting System (RRS) and open the quarterly Financial Data Return / LICAT (life) or MCT (P&C) return for the filing period.
Enter the certified reserve figures into the prescribed schedule lines, matching the GL-posted balance.
Run the RRS built-in validation edits and resolve any flagged inconsistencies before submission.
Submit the return and retain the RRS submission confirmation and timestamp.
checklist.done: the certified reserves are entered into the correct RRS schedule, pass validation edits, and the submission confirmation is retained.

checklist.step: Present the reserve result to the Board Audit & Risk Committee
actions: Upload the valuation memo summary and reserve movement analysis to the board portal ahead of the Audit & Risk Committee meeting.
Brief the Appointed Actuary to attend and answer committee questions on methodology and adequacy.
Record committee questions and the Appointed Actuary's responses in the meeting minutes.
File the approved board minute extract with the valuation record.
checklist.done: the reserve result is presented to and received by the Audit & Risk Committee with minutes filed against the valuation record.

checklist.step: Archive the valuation workpapers
actions: Assemble the full workpaper set (data extract, assumption log, run logs, peer review checklist, reconciliation, memo, sign-offs) into a single valuation package.
Upload the package to the compliance evidence repository under the valuation date and product group.
Apply the 7-year retention label required for actuarial valuation records.
Confirm the package is indexed and searchable by valuation date and legal entity.
checklist.done: the complete workpaper package is archived, retention-labelled and indexed by valuation date and entity.

checklist.step: Set the next cycle's valuation calendar and reminders
actions: Update the valuation calendar with the next quarter-end and year-end valuation dates and the 180-day Appointed Actuary's Report deadline.
Configure calendar reminders at T-60 and T-30 days before each filing deadline to the Appointed Actuary, Chief Actuary and Regulatory Reporting Analyst.
Confirm the reminder distribution list is current after any team change.
checklist.done: the next cycle's deadlines are calendared with T-60/T-30 reminders configured to the current owner list.

testing.step: Build the population of valuation runs performed in the review period
actions: Extract from the model governance repository every quarterly and year-end valuation run completed in the period, by legal entity and product group.
Reconcile the run count to the GL close calendar and the RRS filing calendar for the same period.
Resolve any missing or duplicate run before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the close and filing calendars and signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile each posted reserve to a signed certification memo
actions: Match each population row to a signed valuation memorandum on file.
Check the memo signature date precedes the GL posting date.
List unmatched or unsigned rows as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a pre-dated, signed memorandum or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of the year-end valuation runs and the largest product group by reserve balance in each quarter.
Take 10 additional runs selected at random (seeded, reproducible) from the remaining population.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers 100% of year-end runs and the largest product group each quarter.

testing.step: Re-perform the valuation computation for the sampled runs
actions: Reload the locked assumption set and data extract for each sampled run into a parallel model instance.
Re-execute the CALM/IFRS 17 or discounted-central-estimate run independently of the production output.
Compare the re-performed reserve to the certified figure; log any variance beyond tolerance as an exception.
Capture the re-performed run log into the test workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled run is independently re-performed with the variance against the certified figure documented.

testing.step: Test the PfAD/margin selections against CIA-prescribed ranges
actions: Pull the CIA Standards of Practice prescribed PfAD range tables current as of each sampled valuation date.
Confirm the selected PfAD/margin point for each sampled product group falls within the prescribed range.
Flag any selection outside the range or lacking documented rationale as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled PfAD/margin selection is confirmed within the prescribed range or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Trace the GL-posted reserve to the RRS-filed figure
actions: For each sampled run, open the corresponding OSFI RRS return and locate the filed reserve schedule line.
Compare the RRS-filed figure to the GL-posted balance and the certified valuation memo figure.
Capture the RRS submission confirmation screen into the workpaper.
Log any mismatch as an exception with the dollar difference.
testing.done: every sampled run's RRS-filed figure ties to the GL-posted and certified figures, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Recompute the reserve movement decomposition
actions: For the sampled runs, independently decompose the reserve movement into new business, runoff, assumption change and experience components.
Compare the independent decomposition to the one recorded in the valuation memo.
Log any component that cannot be independently reconciled as an exception.
testing.done: the movement decomposition is independently reproduced and reconciled for every sampled run.

testing.step: Verify peer review and reconciliation evidence exists for every sampled run
actions: Confirm a signed peer review checklist and a Controller-approved GL reconciliation exist for each sampled run.
Confirm the peer reviewer is not the same person who performed the production run.
Log any missing or same-person review as an exception.
testing.done: signed, independent peer review and reconciliation evidence is confirmed for every sampled run.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the run id, entity, product group and the compliance/financial impact.
Assign a root cause (data extract error, assumption drift, model defect, missed reconciliation) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for reserve-deficiency exceptions, notify the Chief Financial Officer.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare it to the zero-tolerance certification/reconciliation threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who performed none of the sampled re-performances, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Audit & Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Compile the valuation basis and change summary for the opinion
actions: Pull the certified year-end valuation memo and reserve movement decomposition from the Reserving Actuary.
List every methodology or assumption change made in the year and its reserve dollar impact.
Confirm the change list matches the model governance repository's change log for the period.
Draft the change-summary section of the opinion from this reconciled list.
checklist.done: the change summary is drawn from the certified valuation memo and reconciles to the model governance repository's change log.

checklist.step: Draft the Appointed Actuary's Report narrative sections
actions: Draft the AAR sections covering valuation methods, assumptions, data sources and judgments per the CIA Standards of Practice content requirements.
Include the reconciliation of reserves to the general ledger and the reserve adequacy conclusion from the year-end valuation.
Have the Actuarial Analyst compile the supporting exhibits (assumption tables, PfAD ranges, sensitivity results) referenced in the narrative.
Cross-check every exhibit reference number against the actual attached exhibit.
checklist.done: the AAR narrative is drafted with every referenced exhibit attached and cross-checked.

checklist.step: Assemble the supporting exhibit package
actions: Pull the final valuation run log, assumption version tags and PfAD tables from the model governance repository.
Format each exhibit with a title, date and version tag matching the AAR narrative reference.
Compile the exhibits into a single package in submission order.
Route the package to the Appointed Actuary for review.
checklist.done: the exhibit package is complete, version-tagged and matches the AAR's exhibit references.

checklist.step: Obtain independent actuarial peer review of the draft opinion
actions: Read the full AAR draft and Statement of the Appointed Actuary against the CIA Standards of Practice content checklist.
Confirm the stated methodology matches the actual model run and that every judgment call is documented with rationale.
Raise review comments in writing and require the Appointed Actuary to resolve each before proceeding.
Sign and date the peer review checklist once all comments are resolved.
checklist.done: a signed peer review checklist exists with every comment resolved before the opinion advances.

checklist.step: Reconfirm the Appointed Actuary's fit-and-proper qualification

Confirm the individual continues to meet the integrity, competence and financial-soundness criteria under the Corporate Governance Guideline.
Record the reconfirmation date and evidence in the governance file.
Notify OSFI of any change to the Appointed Actuary designation per the Guideline E-15 notification requirement.
checklist.done: the Appointed Actuary's fit-and-proper status is reconfirmed and evidenced in the governance file for the current cycle.

checklist.step: Route the draft opinion through Legal/Compliance review
actions: Read the draft opinion and AAR for consistency with the required regulatory language and prior-year filed language.
Confirm no forward-looking or qualifying statements are included that would weaken the certification.
Return comments to the Appointed Actuary in writing with a turnaround deadline.
Sign off that the opinion language is regulator-ready.
checklist.done: Regulatory Counsel has signed off that the opinion language is complete and regulator-ready.

checklist.step: Present the draft opinion to the Chief Actuary
actions: Review the peer-reviewed, legally-cleared draft opinion and AAR in full.
Confirm the capital impact of the certified reserves is consistent with the CFO-approved figures from the valuation sign-off.
Raise any final questions to the Appointed Actuary and require resolution before board presentation.
Approve the draft for board presentation.
checklist.done: the Chief Actuary has approved the draft opinion for board presentation with no open questions.

checklist.step: Present the opinion to the Board Audit & Risk Committee
actions: Upload the draft opinion, AAR summary and peer review outcome to the board portal ahead of the committee meeting.
Have the Appointed Actuary present the opinion and answer committee questions on methodology and adequacy.
Record the committee's acknowledgment and any requested follow-up in the minutes.
File the minute extract with the opinion record.
checklist.done: the committee has acknowledged the opinion with minutes filed against the opinion record.

checklist.step: Sign the Statement of the Appointed Actuary
actions: Confirm every prior step (peer review, legal clearance, Chief Actuary approval, board presentation) is closed with evidence on file.
Sign and date the Statement of the Appointed Actuary certifying the reserves are appropriate under the applicable standards.
Sign and date the accompanying AAR.
Record the signature date on the opinion tracker.
checklist.done: the Statement of the Appointed Actuary and the AAR are signed and dated with all prerequisite evidence on file.

checklist.step: Notarize and version-lock the signed opinion
actions: Confirm the signature is properly executed per the entity's signing authority requirements.
Apply the corporate seal or notarization where the filing jurisdiction requires it.
Lock the signed PDF as the final version and record its checksum in the opinion tracker.
Distribute the locked final version to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst for filing.
checklist.done: the signed opinion is properly executed, version-locked, and handed to the filer.

checklist.step: Attach the opinion to the annual statement package

Insert the signed opinion and AAR into the annual statement package in the position OSFI's Annual Return instructions require.
Verify the package's cross-references (page numbers, exhibit numbers) between the opinion and the financial statements.
Hand the assembled package to the filing owner for submission.
checklist.done: the signed opinion is correctly positioned in the annual statement package with cross-references verified.

checklist.step: Distribute the signed opinion to the external auditor

Respond to any auditor query on methodology by routing it to the Appointed Actuary with a tracked deadline.
Confirm the auditor's management letter carries no unresolved actuarial opinion findings.
File the auditor's acknowledgment with the opinion record.
checklist.done: the external auditor has received the signed opinion and confirmed no unresolved findings remain.

checklist.step: Track the opinion through to OSFI filing
actions: Confirm with the Regulatory Reporting Analyst that the annual statement package including the opinion has been submitted via OSFI's Regulatory Reporting System.
Retain the RRS submission confirmation referencing the opinion attachment.
Update the opinion tracker status to 'Filed' with the submission date and confirmation number.
Notify the Appointed Actuary and Chief Actuary that filing is complete.
checklist.done: the opinion tracker shows 'Filed' with the RRS confirmation number and date.

Upload the record to the compliance evidence repository under the fiscal year and legal entity.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the record is indexed and searchable by opinion date and entity.
checklist.done: the complete opinion record is archived, retention-labelled and indexed by fiscal year and entity.

Configure T-90/T-60/T-30 day reminders to the Appointed Actuary, Chief Actuary and Regulatory Counsel.
Confirm the reminder distribution list is current after any personnel change.
checklist.done: next cycle's deadline is calendared with T-90/T-60/T-30 reminders configured to the current owner list.

Resolve any missing entity before sampling.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the required filing entity list and is signed as complete by the extractor.

Check both evidence items pre-date the opinion signature date.
List unmatched or unsigned items as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every opinion is matched to pre-dated peer review and legal clearance evidence or listed as an exception.

actions: Take 100% of opinions given the annual, low-volume population.
Record the population size and test date in the workpaper.
testing.done: 100% of the opinion population is included in the test with the population size documented.

actions: Pull the Appointed Actuary's CIA membership and continuing-education record as of the opinion date.
Compare to the governance file's fit-and-proper reconfirmation evidence for the same period.
Log any lapse in qualification or missing reconfirmation as an exception.
testing.done: fit-and-proper status is confirmed current as of the opinion date for every entity, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the content check against the CIA Standards of Practice checklist
actions: Independently read each opinion against the current CIA Standards of Practice AAR content requirements.
Confirm methodology, assumptions, data sources and judgments are each addressed with supporting exhibits.
Log any missing required content element as an exception.
testing.done: each opinion is independently confirmed to satisfy the current CIA content requirements or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Confirm board presentation occurred before signature
actions: Pull the Audit & Risk Committee minutes from the board portal for the period preceding each opinion's signature date.
Confirm the minutes record the opinion's presentation and any committee questions and responses.
Log any opinion signed without a preceding board presentation as an exception.
testing.done: board presentation before signature is confirmed for every opinion or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Trace the filed opinion to the OSFI RRS submission
actions: Open the OSFI RRS submission record for the annual statement package and confirm the opinion attachment matches the signed final version by checksum.
Confirm the submission date is on or before the 180-day fiscal-year-end deadline.
Capture the RRS confirmation screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: the filed opinion matches the signed final version and was submitted on or before the 180-day deadline.

testing.step: Recompute the 180-day deadline for every entity
actions: For each entity, recompute the 180-day deadline from its fiscal year-end date.
Compare the recomputed deadline to the actual RRS submission date.
Log any late submission as a reportable exception, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: the 180-day deadline is recomputed and compared to the actual filing date for every entity, with any breach logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with entity, opinion date, what was missed and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause (qualification lapse, missed peer review, late board presentation, late filing) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for a missed statutory deadline, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted none of the sampled opinions, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Audit & Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Confirm all annual statement components are final
actions: Request final, audited financial statements from the Controller and confirm the audit opinion is unqualified or that any qualification is understood and disclosed.
Request the signed actuarial opinion and AAR from the Appointed Actuary.
Request the completed capital return (LICAT or MCT) from the Capital Model Actuary.
Log each component's receipt date on the filing tracker.
checklist.done: all three components (financial statements, opinion/AAR, capital return) are received and logged as final.

checklist.step: Cross-check figures for consistency across the package
actions: Compare the reserve figure in the actuarial opinion to the reserve line in the audited financial statements.
Compare the capital ratio inputs in the LICAT/MCT return to the capital figures in the financial statements.
Flag and route any discrepancy to the Controller and Appointed Actuary for resolution before assembly continues.
Record the cross-check completion on the filing tracker.
checklist.done: all cross-checked figures agree across the package or discrepancies are resolved before assembly.

checklist.step: Assemble the annual statement package in OSFI's required format
actions: Order the package per OSFI's Annual Return instructions: financial statements, notes, capital return, actuarial opinion, AAR.
Insert cross-reference page numbers between the opinion and the financial statement notes it certifies.
Run a completeness checklist against the OSFI Annual Return instructions to confirm no required schedule is missing.
Save the assembled package with a version tag in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the assembled package passes the OSFI completeness checklist and is version-tagged in the repository.

checklist.step: Obtain internal sign-off to file
actions: Review the assembled package summary and the cross-check resolution log.
Confirm with the Chief Actuary that the opinion figures are unchanged from the certified valuation.
Provide written sign-off authorizing submission.
Log the sign-off date on the filing tracker.
checklist.done: the CFO has signed off in writing to authorize submission before the RRS filing step begins.

checklist.step: Log in to OSFI's Regulatory Reporting System and open the filing shell
actions: Log in to OSFI's Regulatory Reporting System (RRS) using the entity's filer credentials.
Open the Annual Return filing shell for the correct legal entity and fiscal year-end.
Confirm the pre-populated entity details (NAIC-equivalent OSFI institution code, fiscal year-end date) are correct.
Begin the upload session and note the session id on the filing tracker.
checklist.done: the correct entity's filing shell is open in RRS with the session id logged.

checklist.step: Upload the package components into RRS
actions: Upload the financial statements, capital return and actuarial opinion/AAR as separate attachments in the RRS schedules they belong to.
Run RRS's built-in validation edits on each schedule and resolve any flagged formatting or completeness error.
Confirm every required RRS field shows a green/valid status before proceeding.
Save the filing as a draft and route it to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for a pre-submission check.
checklist.done: every RRS schedule passes validation and the draft filing is saved for pre-submission review.

checklist.step: Perform the pre-submission review
actions: Open the draft RRS filing and compare each uploaded attachment against the final assembled package for completeness.
Confirm the CFO sign-off date and the actuarial opinion signature date both pre-date today.
Check the filing deadline (180 days from fiscal year-end) has not passed and record days-to-deadline remaining.
Approve the draft for submission or return it with specific corrections.
checklist.done: the pre-submission review is approved with the deadline countdown recorded, or corrections are returned.

checklist.step: Submit the filing in RRS
actions: Submit the approved draft filing in RRS.
Capture the RRS submission confirmation number, submission timestamp and confirming screen.
Download the RRS acknowledgment receipt once issued.
Update the filing tracker status to 'Submitted' with the confirmation number.
checklist.done: the filing is submitted with a captured confirmation number, timestamp and downloaded acknowledgment.

checklist.step: Distribute the filing confirmation internally
actions: Send the RRS confirmation and acknowledgment to the CFO, Chief Actuary and Appointed Actuary.
Notify the Corporate Secretary so the filing can be referenced in the next board meeting materials.
Update the enterprise filing calendar to show the current year's obligation as closed.
checklist.done: the confirmation is distributed to all accountable owners and the filing calendar is updated.

checklist.step: Reconcile the RRS-accepted filing back to the source package
actions: Re-open the accepted filing in RRS and download the system-of-record copy of each schedule.
Byte-for-byte or checksum-compare the RRS-held copy to the internally archived final package.
Log and correct any mismatch through an RRS amendment filing if found.
Record the reconciliation result on the filing tracker.
checklist.done: the RRS-held filing is confirmed identical to the internally archived package, or a corrective amendment is filed.

checklist.step: Handle any OSFI filing-completeness query
actions: Monitor the RRS message center and the designated OSFI liaison mailbox for completeness or clarification queries.
Route any query to the relevant source owner (Controller, Appointed Actuary, Capital Model Actuary) with a response deadline.
Have Regulatory Counsel review any substantive response before it is sent back through RRS.
Log the query and response on the filing tracker.
checklist.done: every OSFI completeness query is logged, routed, reviewed by Regulatory Counsel where substantive, and answered within its deadline.

checklist.step: Report the filing status to the Board
actions: Add the annual statement filing confirmation to the next board meeting's governance report on the board portal.
Note the submission date relative to the 180-day deadline.
Record the board's acknowledgment in the minutes.
checklist.done: the filing status is reported to and acknowledged by the Board with minutes on file.

checklist.step: Archive the filed package and confirmations
actions: Move the final filed package, RRS confirmation, acknowledgment receipt and any query correspondence into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the filing date.
Confirm the record is indexed by legal entity and fiscal year.
checklist.done: the filed package and all confirmations are archived, retention-labelled and indexed.

checklist.step: Update the filing playbook with lessons learned
actions: Note any RRS validation issue, cross-check discrepancy or timeline pressure encountered this cycle.
Update the Annual Statement Filing Procedure with the fix or process change.
Circulate the updated procedure to the filing team ahead of next year's cycle.
checklist.done: the filing procedure is updated with this cycle's lessons and circulated to the team.

checklist.step: Set the next cycle's filing calendar and reminders
actions: Load next fiscal year-end and the resulting 180-day deadline into the filing tracker.
Configure T-90/T-60/T-30/T-10 day reminders to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst, CFO and Appointed Actuary.
Confirm the reminder list is current after any personnel change.
checklist.done: next cycle's deadline is calendared with reminders configured to the current owner list.

testing.step: Build the population of annual statement filings submitted in the review period
actions: Extract from OSFI's RRS filing history every Annual Return submission in the period, by legal entity.
Reconcile the count to the required filing entity list.
Resolve any missing entity before sampling.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the required filing entity list and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile each filing to its CFO sign-off
actions: Match each filing to a written CFO sign-off authorizing submission.
Check the sign-off date pre-dates the RRS submission timestamp.
List unmatched filings as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every filing is matched to a pre-dated CFO sign-off or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of filings given the annual, low-volume population across entities.
Record the population size and test date in the workpaper.
testing.done: 100% of the filing population is included with the population size documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the completeness check against OSFI's Annual Return instructions
actions: Independently pull the current OSFI Annual Return completeness checklist.
Open each sampled filing in RRS and confirm every required schedule and attachment is present.
Log any missing schedule or attachment as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled filing is independently confirmed complete against the current OSFI checklist or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Verify cross-check figures agree across the filed package
actions: Compare the reserve figure in the filed opinion to the reserve line in the filed financial statements for each sampled filing.
Compare the capital return inputs to the filed financial statement capital figures.
Log any unresolved discrepancy as an exception.
testing.done: cross-check figures are confirmed to agree across every sampled filed package or discrepancies are logged.

testing.step: Trace the RRS submission to the internally archived final package
actions: Download the RRS-held copy of each sampled filing's attachments.
Checksum-compare to the version archived in the compliance evidence repository.
Log any mismatch as an exception and confirm whether an amendment filing was made.
testing.done: the RRS-held filing is confirmed identical to the archived package for every sampled filing, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Recompute the 180-day filing deadline for every sampled entity
actions: Recompute the 180-day deadline from each entity's fiscal year-end date.
Compare the recomputed deadline to the actual RRS submission timestamp.
Log any late submission as a reportable exception.
testing.done: the 180-day deadline is recomputed and compared to the actual filing date for every sampled entity.

testing.step: Confirm board reporting of the filing status occurred
actions: Pull the board minutes from the board portal for the period following each sampled filing.
Confirm the filing status was reported and acknowledged.
Log any missing board report as an exception.
testing.done: board reporting of the filing status is confirmed for every sampled filing or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the entity, filing date, what was missed and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause (missing schedule, cross-check gap, late submission, missed board report) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for a missed statutory deadline, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who assembled and submitted none of the sampled filings, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Audit & Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Refresh the asset and liability inventory
actions: Pull the current investment portfolio holdings from the Chief Investment Officer's asset system and the current in-force liability extract from the actuarial modeling platform.
Reconcile total asset market value and liability reserve totals to the general ledger.
Update the asset/liability inventory record in the model governance repository with the refreshed totals and as-of date.
Flag any newly acquired asset class or product line that lacks a modeled cash-flow profile.
checklist.done: the asset/liability inventory is refreshed, GL-reconciled, and any unmodeled new class or product is flagged.

checklist.step: Design the base scenario and the prescribed adverse scenarios
actions: Set the base scenario using current best-estimate assumptions consistent with the year-end valuation.
Design the prescribed adverse scenarios per CIA Standards of Practice: interest rate rise/fall, mortality/morbidity deterioration, lapse deterioration, expense increase, and reduced new business.
Size each adverse scenario's shock magnitude against CIA guidance and document the rationale.
Have the Chief Actuary approve the final scenario set before scenario runs begin.
checklist.done: the base and all prescribed adverse scenarios are designed, sized against CIA guidance, and approved by the Chief Actuary.

checklist.step: Configure and run the projection model for each scenario
actions: Load the refreshed asset/liability inventory and the approved scenario set into the FIS Prophet asset-liability projection module.
Run the base scenario and each adverse scenario over the minimum 3-year projection horizon.
Capture surplus/deficiency and capital ratio trajectories for each scenario run.
Save each run log with scenario name, model version and run date to the model governance repository.
checklist.done: every approved scenario is run over the required horizon with surplus/capital trajectories captured and logged.

checklist.step: Analyze scenario results for ruin points and capital breaches
actions: Review each scenario's projected surplus and capital ratio path for any point where capital falls below the internal target or the OSFI supervisory target.
Where a breach occurs, identify the projection year, magnitude and the driving assumption.
Document management actions that would plausibly be taken before the breach point (assumed only where consistent with CIA guidance on credible actions).
Summarize each scenario's outcome in a results table.
checklist.done: every scenario's outcome, including any capital breach point and driving assumption, is documented in a results table.

checklist.step: Draft the Financial Condition Testing report
actions: Draft the FCT report covering scenario design rationale, results table, ruin analysis, and the overall financial condition opinion.
Reference the refreshed asset/liability inventory and cite the CIA Standards of Practice sections applied.
Attach the run logs and scenario assumption documentation as exhibits.
State an explicit conclusion on the entity's financial condition over the projection horizon.
checklist.done: a draft FCT report with results, ruin analysis, exhibits and an explicit financial-condition conclusion exists.

checklist.step: Obtain independent peer review of the FCT report
actions: Independently re-run at least two of the prescribed adverse scenarios in a parallel model instance.
Compare results to the draft report's figures and log any variance beyond tolerance as a review finding.
Confirm every prescribed CIA scenario category is addressed in the report.
Sign and date the peer review checklist.
checklist.done: a peer reviewer has independently reproduced at least two adverse scenarios within tolerance and signed the review checklist.

checklist.step: Reconcile FCT model inputs to the certified year-end valuation
actions: Compare the base scenario's opening reserves and assets to the certified year-end valuation memo figures.
Investigate and document any difference beyond the materiality threshold.
Confirm the assumption set used in the base scenario matches the locked valuation assumption version.
Sign off that FCT inputs tie to the certified valuation.
checklist.done: FCT base-scenario inputs are confirmed to tie to the certified year-end valuation within tolerance.

checklist.step: Route the draft FCT report to the Chief Actuary
actions: Review the peer-reviewed draft FCT report and the valuation reconciliation.
Assess whether any capital breach point warrants an immediate capital management action ahead of board reporting.
Approve the draft for board presentation or return it with required changes.
Log the approval date on the FCT tracker.
checklist.done: the Chief Actuary has approved the draft FCT report for board presentation.

checklist.step: Present the FCT results to the Board Audit & Risk Committee
actions: Upload the FCT report and results summary to the board portal ahead of the committee meeting.
Have the Appointed Actuary present the scenario results, any capital breach points and management action assumptions.
Record committee questions and responses, and any requested capital management follow-up, in the minutes.
File the minute extract with the FCT record.
checklist.done: the FCT results are presented to and received by the committee with minutes filed against the FCT record.

checklist.step: Escalate any projected capital breach to capital management
actions: Review any scenario showing a projected breach of the internal or OSFI supervisory capital target.
Convene the capital management team to assess mitigating actions (reinsurance, capital raise, in-force management).
Document the chosen mitigating action and its expected capital impact.
Report the escalation and action plan to the Chief Risk Officer.
checklist.done: any projected capital breach has a documented, CFO-reviewed mitigating action plan reported to the Chief Risk Officer.

checklist.step: Finalize and sign the FCT report
actions: Incorporate any board or Chief Actuary feedback into the final FCT report.
Confirm all exhibits and the peer review checklist are attached in the final version.
Sign and date the final FCT report.
Lock the final PDF version with a checksum reference in the FCT tracker.
checklist.done: the final FCT report is signed, dated and version-locked with all exhibits attached.

checklist.step: Reference the FCT conclusion in the Appointed Actuary's Report
actions: Insert a summary of the FCT scenario results and financial-condition conclusion into the relevant AAR section.
Cross-reference the AAR entry to the full FCT report exhibit number.
Confirm the AAR's overall reserve adequacy statement is consistent with the FCT conclusion.
Flag any inconsistency to the Chief Actuary before the AAR is signed.
checklist.done: the AAR references the FCT conclusion consistently, with any inconsistency resolved before AAR signature.

checklist.step: Update the FCT model and scenario change log
actions: Record the FCT model version, scenario library version and any methodology change in the model governance repository.
Tag each change with the approver and the date.
Cross-reference to the FCT report exhibit number.
Flag any change requiring model risk validation before next use.
checklist.done: every FCT model/scenario change is logged, tagged, cross-referenced and flagged for validation where required.

checklist.step: Archive the FCT report and workpapers
actions: Assemble the signed FCT report, scenario assumptions, run logs, peer review checklist and board minutes into a single package.
Upload the package to the compliance evidence repository under the fiscal year and legal entity.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the package is indexed and searchable by fiscal year and entity.
checklist.done: the complete FCT package is archived, retention-labelled and indexed by fiscal year and entity.

checklist.step: Set the next cycle's FCT calendar and reminders
actions: Load the next fiscal year-end into the FCT tracker with milestone dates for scenario design, run completion and board presentation.
Configure reminders at T-120 (design), T-60 (run completion) and T-30 (board presentation) days before year-end.
Confirm the reminder distribution list is current after any personnel change.
checklist.done: next cycle's FCT milestones are calendared with reminders configured to the current owner list.

testing.step: Build the population of FCT scenario runs performed in the review period
actions: Extract from the model governance repository every FCT scenario run for the review period, by legal entity and scenario category.
Reconcile the count of scenarios run to the CIA-prescribed minimum scenario set.
Resolve any missing prescribed scenario before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the CIA-prescribed minimum scenario set and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the FCT report to the asset/liability inventory refresh
actions: Confirm the FCT report's opening asset and liability totals match the refreshed inventory record for the same as-of date.
Check the inventory refresh date pre-dates the scenario run dates.
List any unreconciled or stale inventory as an exception.
testing.done: the FCT report's opening balances tie to a current, pre-dated inventory refresh or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of the prescribed adverse scenario categories (interest rate, mortality/morbidity, lapse, expense, new business).
Take the base scenario plus 2 additional scenario runs at random for full re-performance.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers 100% of prescribed scenario categories plus a reproducible random re-performance set.

testing.step: Re-perform the sampled scenario runs
actions: Reload the locked scenario assumptions and inventory into a parallel model instance.
Re-execute each sampled scenario independently of the production run.
Compare the re-performed surplus/capital trajectory to the reported figures and log any variance beyond tolerance.
Capture the re-performed run log into the test workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled scenario is independently re-performed with the variance against the reported figures documented.

testing.step: Check the scenario shock sizing against CIA guidance
actions: Pull the current CIA Standards of Practice guidance on adverse scenario shock magnitudes.
Compare each sampled adverse scenario's shock size to the guidance range.
Flag any scenario sized outside the guidance range without documented rationale as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled scenario's shock sizing is confirmed against CIA guidance or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Verify the FCT base scenario ties to the certified year-end valuation
actions: Compare the FCT base scenario's opening reserves and assumption set to the certified year-end valuation memo.
Confirm the Valuation Actuary's tie-out sign-off exists and pre-dates the FCT report.
Log any untied figure as an exception.
testing.done: the FCT base scenario is confirmed tied to the certified valuation with a pre-dated sign-off, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Confirm capital breach escalation occurred where projected
actions: Identify any sampled scenario projecting a capital target breach.
Confirm a CFO-reviewed mitigating action plan exists and was reported to the Chief Risk Officer for that breach.
Log any breach without a documented escalation as an exception.
testing.done: every projected capital breach in the sample has a documented, escalated mitigating action or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Confirm board presentation and peer review evidence exists
actions: Pull board minutes from the board portal confirming FCT presentation for the review period.
Confirm a signed peer review checklist exists and pre-dates the Chief Actuary's approval.
Log any missing board presentation or peer review as an exception.
testing.done: board presentation and peer review evidence is confirmed for the review period or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the scenario, entity, what was missed and the compliance/capital impact.
Assign a root cause (stale inventory, missed scenario, sizing gap, missed escalation) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for capital-adequacy exceptions, notify the Chief Risk Officer.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for missing prescribed scenarios.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who performed none of the sampled re-performances, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Audit & Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Pull the policy admin book-of-record extract
actions: Log in to the Policy Administration Platform and run the standard in-force/claims extract as of the quarter-end cutoff.
Capture the control totals (policy count, sum insured, premium in force, claim reserve total) directly from the platform's reporting module.
Save the extract with a timestamped filename and hash it for integrity.
Hand the extract and control totals to the Reserving Actuary.
checklist.done: the book-of-record extract is pulled with control totals captured and a hashed, timestamped file handed off.

checklist.step: Pull the actuarial model's staged extract
actions: Open the actuarial modeling platform's staging area and export the extract loaded for the current valuation cycle.
Capture the same control totals (policy count, sum insured, premium, claim reserve) from the staged extract.
Confirm the staged extract's valuation date matches the policy admin extract's cutoff date exactly.
Hand the staged control totals to the Reserving Actuary.
checklist.done: the staged extract's control totals are captured and confirmed to share the same cutoff date as the book-of-record extract.

checklist.step: Match control totals between the two sources
actions: Compare policy count, sum insured, premium and claim reserve control totals between the book-of-record and staged extracts.
Compute the dollar and percentage variance for each control total.
Flag any variance exceeding the materiality threshold (typically 0.5% of the total) for record-level investigation.
Record the control-total comparison table in the reconciliation report.
checklist.done: control totals are compared with variances computed, and any threshold breach is flagged for record-level investigation.

checklist.step: Perform record-level matching on flagged control totals
actions: Load both extracts into the enterprise data warehouse and join on policy/claim identifier.
Identify unmatched records (present in one source but not the other) and records with a field-level mismatch (sum insured, reserve amount, status).
Categorize each unmatched or mismatched record by likely cause: new business timing, lapse timing, data entry error, or interface defect.
Export the categorized break list to the reconciliation report.
checklist.done: unmatched and mismatched records are identified, categorized by likely cause, and exported to the reconciliation report.

checklist.step: Investigate each material break to a root cause
actions: For each break above the individual materiality threshold, open the source policy or claim record in the Policy Administration Platform and confirm its current status.
Determine whether the break is a timing difference (in-flight transaction), a mapping error, or a genuine data-quality defect.
Document the root cause and the dollar impact on the break log.
Route interface or mapping defects to the Data Engineer for a system-level fix ticket.
checklist.done: every material break has a documented root cause, dollar impact, and a fix ticket where a system defect is the cause.

checklist.step: Correct or accept each break before the extract is used
actions: For timing differences, confirm no correction is needed and document the accepted rationale.
For genuine data errors within the actuary's control, correct the staged extract and re-pull the affected records.
For breaks that cannot be corrected before the valuation deadline, document the dollar impact on reserves and route for sign-off as an accepted limitation.
Update the break log with the final disposition for every break.
checklist.done: every break carries a final disposition (accepted timing difference, corrected, or accepted limitation) before the extract proceeds to valuation.

checklist.step: Quantify the aggregate reconciliation impact on reserves
actions: Sum the reserve dollar impact of all accepted, unresolved breaks.
Compare the aggregate impact to the valuation materiality threshold used in the reserve certification.
Where the aggregate impact exceeds the threshold, flag it for disclosure in the valuation memo.
Record the aggregate impact figure in the reconciliation report.
checklist.done: the aggregate reserve impact of unresolved breaks is quantified and compared to the valuation materiality threshold.

checklist.step: Draft the reconciliation report
actions: Compile the control-total comparison, break log, root causes and dispositions into the quarterly reconciliation report.
State the aggregate reserve impact of unresolved breaks and whether it exceeds the materiality threshold.
Attach the two source extract hashes to prove the extracts used are the ones reconciled.
Route the report for sign-off.
checklist.done: the reconciliation report is compiled with control totals, breaks, dispositions, impact statement and source-extract hashes attached.

checklist.step: Obtain sign-off to proceed to valuation
actions: Confirm every material break carries a final disposition and the aggregate impact is within tolerance, or is explicitly flagged for the valuation memo.
Sign and date the reconciliation report as complete.
Notify the Valuation Actuary that the extract is cleared to proceed into the production valuation run.
Log the sign-off date on the reconciliation tracker.
checklist.done: the reconciliation report is signed and the extract is formally cleared to proceed into valuation.

checklist.step: Route system-level break fixes for follow-through
actions: Open a ticket in the ITSM platform for every interface or mapping defect identified in the reconciliation.
Assign a fix owner and target date, prioritized by the dollar impact of the defect.
Track the ticket through to closure and confirm the fix is verified in the next quarter's reconciliation.
Report open, aged tickets to the Data Quality Manager monthly.
checklist.done: every system-level break has a tracked ticket, and prior-quarter fixes are verified closed in the current reconciliation.

checklist.step: Report unresolved material breaks to the Chief Actuary
actions: Review any break disposition flagged as an accepted limitation with a material reserve impact.
Decide whether the impact requires disclosure in the valuation memo or an adjustment to reserves.
Document the decision and its rationale.
Log the decision on the reconciliation tracker.
checklist.done: every material accepted-limitation break has a Chief Actuary decision on disclosure or adjustment, documented and logged.

checklist.step: Link the reconciliation report to the valuation workpaper
actions: Attach the signed reconciliation report as an exhibit to the current quarter's valuation workpaper.
Cross-reference the aggregate impact figure in the valuation memo's data-quality section.
Confirm the cross-reference page numbers are correct.
Notify the Appointed Actuary that the reconciliation exhibit is attached.
checklist.done: the signed reconciliation report is attached to the valuation workpaper with correct cross-references.

checklist.step: Track reconciliation cycle time and break trends
actions: Log the reconciliation completion date and break count for the quarter on a trend tracker.
Compare break count and dollar impact against the prior four quarters.
Escalate a rising break-count trend to the Reserving Actuary and Data Engineering lead for root-cause review.
Report the trend to the Chief Data Officer quarterly.
checklist.done: reconciliation cycle time and break trends are tracked quarterly with rising trends escalated.

checklist.step: Archive the reconciliation package
actions: Assemble the reconciliation report, break log, source extract hashes and sign-off into a package.
Upload the package to the compliance evidence repository under the valuation date and legal entity.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the package is indexed and searchable by valuation date.
checklist.done: the reconciliation package is archived, retention-labelled and indexed by valuation date.

checklist.step: Set the next quarter's reconciliation calendar and reminders
actions: Load the next quarter-end date and the 3-business-day reconciliation deadline into the reconciliation tracker.
Configure reminders at quarter-end +1 and an escalation alert at +3 if unresolved.
Confirm the reminder distribution list is current after any personnel change.
checklist.done: next quarter's reconciliation deadline is calendared with reminders and an escalation alert configured.

testing.step: Build the population of reconciliations performed in the review period
actions: Extract from the compliance evidence repository every quarterly reconciliation report for the period, by legal entity and product.
Reconcile the count to the number of valuation cycles run in the period.
Resolve any missing reconciliation before sampling.
testing.done: the population reconciles to the number of valuation cycles run and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile each valuation run to a signed, pre-dated reconciliation report
actions: Match each valuation run to a signed reconciliation report.
Check the reconciliation sign-off date pre-dates the valuation run start date.
List unmatched or post-dated reconciliations as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every valuation run is matched to a pre-dated, signed reconciliation report or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take the reconciliation with the largest aggregate break impact from each quarter in the period.
Take 2 additional reconciliations selected at random (seeded, reproducible).
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and includes the largest-impact reconciliation from every quarter.

testing.step: Re-perform the control-total comparison for the sample
actions: Independently re-pull the policy admin control totals for the sampled quarter-end date.
Independently pull the staged extract control totals used in the same valuation run.
Recompute the variance and compare to the reported reconciliation variance.
Log any unexplained difference as an exception.
testing.done: control totals are independently re-pulled and the recomputed variance matches the reported figure or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Re-perform record-level matching on a sub-sample of breaks
actions: Take 15 breaks at random from each sampled reconciliation's break log.
Independently trace each to the source policy admin record and confirm the recorded root cause is accurate.
Log any break whose recorded root cause cannot be independently confirmed as an exception.
testing.done: root causes for the sub-sampled breaks are independently confirmed or logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Test the disposition of every material break
actions: For every break above the materiality threshold in the sample, confirm a final disposition (accepted timing difference, corrected, accepted limitation) is recorded.
For corrected breaks, confirm the corrected extract was actually used in the valuation run.
For accepted-limitation breaks, confirm the Chief Actuary's disclosure/adjustment decision is documented.
Log any break without a complete disposition trail as an exception.
testing.done: every material break in the sample has a confirmed, complete disposition trail or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Verify the aggregate reserve impact figure
actions: Independently sum the dollar impact of unresolved breaks in each sampled reconciliation.
Compare to the aggregate impact figure stated in the reconciliation report.
Log any discrepancy as an exception.
testing.done: the aggregate impact figure is independently recomputed and matches the reported figure or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Confirm the reconciliation exhibit was attached to the valuation workpaper
actions: Open the certified valuation memo for each sampled quarter and confirm the reconciliation report is attached as an exhibit.
Confirm the cross-reference in the memo's data-quality section matches the reconciliation exhibit.
Log any missing or mismatched exhibit as an exception.
testing.done: the reconciliation exhibit is confirmed attached and correctly cross-referenced for every sampled quarter, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the quarter, entity, what was missed and the reserve dollar impact.
Assign a root cause (interface defect, mapping error, missed sign-off, incomplete disposition) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for reserve-impacting exceptions, notify the Chief Actuary.
Carry every open exception into next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare it to the zero-tolerance threshold for unresolved, unsigned-off material breaks.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who performed none of the sampled reconciliations, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Audit & Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Log the incoming OSFI inquiry
actions: Open the OSFI RRS message center (or the designated OSFI liaison mailbox) and identify the new inquiry.
Log the inquiry in the regulatory filing/issue tracker with received date, stated due date, subject and requesting OSFI contact.
Classify the inquiry type: valuation methodology question, data request, follow-up to a prior filing, or examination-related.
Assign a case owner based on classification.
checklist.done: the inquiry is logged with due date, classification and an assigned case owner within 1 business day of receipt.

checklist.step: Route the inquiry to the substantive owner
actions: Route valuation methodology and adequacy questions to the Appointed Actuary.
Route data-specific questions to the Reserving Actuary or Data Quality Analyst as applicable.
Route examination-related inquiries to the Chief Actuary and Regulatory Counsel jointly.
Confirm the case owner has acknowledged receipt within 1 business day.
checklist.done: the inquiry is routed to the correct substantive owner with acknowledged receipt logged.

checklist.step: Research the inquiry against the underlying workpapers
actions: Pull the relevant valuation memo, run logs and assumption documentation from the model governance repository for the period the inquiry concerns.
Reconstruct the specific figure, methodology choice, or data point OSFI is asking about.
Identify whether the answer is a simple clarification or requires new analysis.
Note any gap in existing documentation that the response will need to fill.
checklist.done: the inquiry's underlying facts are reconstructed from workpapers with any documentation gap identified.

checklist.step: Draft the substantive response
actions: Draft a direct answer to each question in the inquiry, referencing the specific workpaper, memo section or exhibit that supports it.
Avoid speculative or forward-looking statements not supported by the record.
Attach or reference supporting exhibits (run logs, assumption tables, reconciliation reports) as needed.
Flag any question the team cannot fully answer within the response window for early escalation.
checklist.done: a draft response answering every inquiry question with cited supporting exhibits exists, with any unanswerable item flagged.

checklist.step: Have a peer actuary review the draft for accuracy
actions: Independently verify each cited figure in the draft response against the source workpaper.
Confirm the response does not contradict any previously filed opinion or return.
Raise any inaccuracy or inconsistency in writing and require it be resolved before the response advances.
Sign off that the draft is factually accurate.
checklist.done: a peer actuary has verified every cited figure and signed off on the draft's accuracy.

checklist.step: Route the draft through Regulatory Counsel review
actions: Read the draft response for tone, scope and any statement that could be read as an admission beyond the facts.
Confirm the response does not disclose information outside the scope of the specific inquiry.
Return comments to the Appointed Actuary with a same-week turnaround.
Sign off that the response is legally clear for submission.
checklist.done: Regulatory Counsel has signed off that the response is scoped correctly and legally clear.

checklist.step: Obtain Chief Actuary approval
actions: Review the peer-reviewed, legally-cleared draft response in full.
Confirm the response is consistent with the entity's most recent certified valuation and AAR.
Approve the response for submission or return it with final changes.
Log the approval date on the inquiry tracker.
checklist.done: the Chief Actuary has approved the response for submission.

checklist.step: Submit the response through the OSFI channel it arrived on
actions: Submit the approved response through the OSFI RRS message center or the channel the inquiry was received on.
Attach every supporting exhibit referenced in the response.
Capture the submission confirmation and timestamp.
Update the inquiry tracker status to 'Responded' with the submission date.
checklist.done: the response is submitted through the correct channel with all exhibits attached and the submission confirmation captured.

checklist.step: Confirm submission before the stated due date
actions: Compare the submission timestamp to the inquiry's stated due date.
Where the response is at risk of missing the due date, request an extension from OSFI in writing before the due date passes.
Log any extension granted, with the new due date, on the inquiry tracker.
Escalate any missed due date to the Chief Actuary and Head of Compliance immediately.
checklist.done: the response's timing against the due date is confirmed, with any extension logged or any miss immediately escalated.

checklist.step: Track any OSFI follow-up question
actions: Monitor the RRS message center for an OSFI follow-up to the submitted response.
Log any follow-up as a linked child inquiry on the tracker, retaining the parent-child relationship.
Route the follow-up through the same research/draft/review/approve/submit cycle.
Close the parent inquiry only once no further follow-up is received within the standard 20-business-day window.
checklist.done: any OSFI follow-up is logged, linked to the parent inquiry, and the parent is closed only after the follow-up window elapses.

checklist.step: Update internal documentation where the inquiry revealed a gap
actions: Where research for the response revealed a documentation gap in the valuation memo or AAR, note the gap.
Update the relevant procedure or workpaper template to close the gap for the next cycle.
Notify the Chief Actuary of the documentation improvement made.
Log the update on the inquiry tracker as a corrective action.
checklist.done: any documentation gap surfaced by the inquiry is closed in the relevant procedure or template, logged as a corrective action.

checklist.step: Notify internal stakeholders of the response outcome
actions: Summarize the inquiry, response and any OSFI reaction for the Chief Risk Officer and Board Governance Lead.
Flag any inquiry pattern suggesting a broader supervisory concern.
Include material inquiries in the next Compliance Committee update.
File the summary with the inquiry record.
checklist.done: material inquiry outcomes are summarized to the Chief Risk Officer and reported to the Compliance Committee.

checklist.step: Archive the complete correspondence file
actions: Assemble the inquiry, research notes, draft versions, peer review sign-off, legal clearance and final submitted response into one file.
Upload the file to the compliance evidence repository under the inquiry date and legal entity.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the file is indexed and searchable by inquiry date and OSFI reference number.
checklist.done: the complete correspondence file is archived, retention-labelled and indexed by inquiry date and reference number.

checklist.step: Review inquiry volume and turnaround trends
actions: Compile inquiry count, average turnaround time and any missed deadlines for the quarter.
Compare trends against the prior four quarters.
Report the trend and any process bottleneck to the Chief Risk Officer.
Adjust the response SLA or staffing if turnaround is consistently at risk.
checklist.done: inquiry volume and turnaround trends are compiled, reported, and any needed process adjustment is made.

checklist.step: Confirm the response procedure is current
actions: Review the Regulator Inquiry Response Procedure annually against actual practice observed in the period.
Update routing rules, SLA windows or escalation triggers as needed.
Circulate the updated procedure to all case owners.
Log the review date and any changes made.
checklist.done: the response procedure is reviewed annually, updated where needed, and circulated to case owners.

testing.step: Build the population of OSFI inquiries received in the review period
actions: Extract from the RRS message center and the regulatory filing/issue tracker every OSFI inquiry received in the period.
Reconcile the tracker count to the RRS message center count.
Resolve any discrepancy before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled between the tracker and RRS message center and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile each inquiry to a logged response
actions: Match each inquiry to a submitted response on the tracker.
Check the response submission date against the inquiry's stated due date.
List any inquiry without a matched response, or with a late response, as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every inquiry is matched to a response with timeliness checked, or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of examination-related inquiries.
Take 5 additional inquiries selected at random (seeded, reproducible) from the remaining population.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers 100% of examination-related inquiries.

testing.step: Re-verify the accuracy of each sampled response
actions: Independently pull the source workpaper cited in each sampled response.
Confirm every figure and methodology statement in the response matches the source workpaper.
Log any inaccuracy or unsupported statement as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled response's figures are independently confirmed against source workpapers or logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Confirm peer review and legal clearance evidence exists
actions: Confirm a signed peer actuary accuracy sign-off exists for each sampled response.
Confirm a Regulatory Counsel clearance sign-off exists and pre-dates submission.
Log any missing sign-off as an exception.
testing.done: peer review and legal clearance evidence is confirmed present and pre-dated for every sampled response, or logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Trace each response to its OSFI submission confirmation
actions: Open the RRS message center and locate the submission confirmation for each sampled response.
Confirm the submitted content matches the final approved draft on file.
Capture the confirmation screen into the workpaper.
Log any mismatch as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled response's submission is traced to a matching RRS confirmation or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Recompute response timeliness against the stated due date
actions: For each sampled inquiry, recompute the business days between receipt and response submission.
Compare to the due date stated in the original inquiry (or any documented extension).
Log any late response as a reportable exception, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: response timeliness is recomputed and compared to the due date (or extension) for every sampled inquiry.

testing.step: Confirm follow-up inquiries were tracked to closure
actions: For sampled inquiries with a logged follow-up, confirm the follow-up went through the same review cycle as the parent.
Confirm the parent inquiry was closed only after the follow-up window elapsed with no further question.
Log any inquiry closed prematurely as an exception.
testing.done: follow-up handling and closure timing is confirmed correct for every sampled inquiry with a follow-up, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the inquiry id, what was missed and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause (missed routing, late review, inaccurate content, late submission) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for a missed statutory-style deadline, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance timeliness/review threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted none of the sampled responses, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.
